title: I tore down my whole cyberpunk street and rebuilt it in 3D. Before vs. after, made with just Opus and ChatGPT
author: the_builder_ai
selftext:
Two months ago I started building a game and wanted to make something fun with a real story. I went through a bunch of prototypes until one finally clicked - a 2.5D cyberpunk side-scroller in a rain-soaked neon city. The colors, the reflections, the mood once the music came in, that was the one, so I built the whole city. 

Opus made the buildings out of rectangular blocks, and I had ChatGPT generate facades to paste onto them. Honestly, it looked pretty good (left side of the video). I was happy with it. Then I tried a quick prototype where the buildings had proper depth, and I loved it. The old version suddenly looked more like painted boxes.

Switching meant redoing the entire street but I thought, why not. I tore everything down and had Opus 5.5 rebuild it from scratch, this time with signs and billboards sticking out, AC units, awnings, and recessed doorways. Same street, but now it feels lived in.

The hardest part was placement. It’s really hard to tell an AI to move a sign two inches to the left, and getting everything to sit right took a lot of back and forth.

**How it’s built:** Opus 5.5 blocks out every building in plain geometry (the pink section in the video), ChatGPT generates the facade art, and Opus builds the 3D details on top. That’s the whole stack. Opus can code everything, from the gameplay to even video editing. ChatGPT is only used to generate building images. No other external assets used or anything generated with Tripo/MeshyAI.

What do you guys think of the gameplay view? Would you have rebuilt it too? If you’re working on a 2.5D game like this or a side-scroller in general, happy to go deeper on the workflow in the comments.

This is my [first post on this game](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1x7dzo9/started_as_a_quick_prototype_to_test_opus_55_and/) if you want to see where it started. Quick note: camera in the actual game will be closer but I wanted to zoom out to show a better view of the upgraded buildings. Welcome any comments or discussion!

comments.author: Daniel_Mitchell24
comments.body: i think the rebuilt was worth it the added depth makes the street feel more alive adn i'm curious how it'll look with the camera closer during actual gameplay

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body:
I'm testing different angles (more top down vs. street view) and also zoom (more character vs. more environment). I think both have their own strengths - zoomed out allows the player to take in the environment more with all the different details while zoomed in makes the player feel closer to combat. Probably will allow different zoom scrolling, but here's a closer view. I think the screenshot makes it look smaller but in this view the character is almost 1/3 to 1/4 of the screen so he's much closer!

https://i.redd.it/m0s1aky6uezh1.png

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body:
Hey, thanks for taking a look! Appreciate you reaching out and happy to learn more about the platform.

The idea of the platform is really interesting but for a bit of context - as the current game stands, it has a several-hour campaign across six chapters, with story cutscenes and minigames, which probably isn’t obvious from this clip! Do you see longer games like that fitting on the platform too?

replies.author: Low_Imagination_9670
replies.body: I do indeed! What's the size of the current build?

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body: It is hovering around \~700 mb now but there's room to optimize with the video and sprite sheets. I've been upscaling the bosses to look better but those have room to improve.

replies.author: Low_Imagination_9670
replies.body: Yeah this size is quite prohibitive for a browser game that loads at parties, curious how compact you can get it.

replies.body: Yes that's right. I think one of the best lessons I learned is that don't ever get comfortable or fall into a specific routine. The way I work with models now are completely different from how I used just 3-4 months ago. Be adaptive
